title: Quantum-enhanced Search for Galactic Dark Photons Using Cat-State Cavities
authors: Aoying Wang, Yanjie Zeng, Yanyan Cai, Jing Shu, Bin Xu, Yuan Xu, Pan Zheng
abstract: We present a quantum-enhanced search for the Galactic dark-photon background (GDPB), a relativistic and anisotropic vector field that can be produced by dark-matter decay or annihilation in the Milky Way halo. We reinterpret an existing quantum-enhanced dark-photon dataset obtained with a superconducting circuit QED platform originally developed for wave-like dark-photon dark-matter searches, consisting of a high-$Q$ niobium cavity in the $\mathrm{TM}_{010}$ mode dispersively coupled to a transmon qubit. By preparing four-component cat states and performing repeated quantum non-demolition parity measurements, analyzed with a hidden Markov model, we extract photon-transition probabilities for multiple cat amplitudes and integration times. The coupling to the GDPB is governed by a polarization- and angle-dependent cavity overlap function, which predicts a distinctive diurnal modulation of the excitation rate for both longitudinal and transverse polarizations. From the absence of such modulation, we set 90\% confidence-level bounds on the kinetic-mixing parameter $ε$ for two benchmark production mechanisms (parametric and cascade decay) over the relativistic mass range $m_X \ll ω_c$.
summary: This paper details a quantum-enhanced experimental search for the Galactic Dark Photon Background (GDPB) using a superconducting circuit QED platform. By preparing the cavity in cat states and analyzing the expected diurnal modulation due to the anisotropic dark matter field, the authors constrain the dark photon mixing parameter $\epsilon$. The work demonstrates the utility of quantum state engineering for next-generation searches in fundamental physics.
main_problem: The paper aims to conduct a quantum-enhanced search for the Galactic Dark Photon Background (GDPB), a relativistic and anisotropic vector field potentially sourced by dark matter decay or annihilation in the Milky Way.
main_result: By analyzing the diurnal modulation of the excitation rate, the authors set 90% confidence-level upper bounds on the kinetic-mixing parameter $\epsilon$ for two benchmark dark photon production mechanisms.
method: The analysis reinterprets existing quantum-enhanced data using superconducting circuit QED (cQED) measurements, employing a hidden Markov model to extract photon-transition probabilities.
model_or_system: The system is a high-Q niobium cavity dispersively coupled to a transmon qubit, utilizing four-component cat states for quantum enhancement. The signal interaction is governed by the coupling to the anisotropic GDPB, which introduces a polarization- and angle-dependent cavity overlap function.
key_observables: Diurnal modulation of the excitation rate, measured positive-event fraction ($n_{	ext{meas}}$), and the normalized excitation rate ($R_i$).
important_parameters: Kinetic-mixing parameter $\epsilon$, relativistic mass range $m_X \ll \omega_c$, and the cavity overlap function $C_P(\hat{k})$ dependent on the incidence angle $\Psi(t)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the use of the $\mathrm{TM}_{010}$ mode and relies on statistical approximations (Gaussian distribution) for background subtraction and limit setting.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the schematic of the anisotropic GDPB, the cQED setup, and the polarization-dependent cavity overlap. Figure 5 presents the final 90% credible upper limits on $\epsilon$ versus $m_X$.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical model (GDPB signal, cQED detector) and the necessary quantum enhancement techniques using cat states. It details the methodology involving directional overlap functions and diurnal modulation analysis. Finally, it presents the statistical framework for setting upper bounds on the mixing parameter $\epsilon$ based on the absence of a signal.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it applies advanced quantum sensing techniques (cat states, cavity QED) to search for fundamental physics signals (dark photons), providing a concrete example of how quantum information principles enhance experimental sensitivity in AMO/Quantum Optics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Schematic of an anisotropic GDPB produced by dark-matter decay or annihilation in the Milky Way halo. Earth’s rotation changes the cavity axis ˆlcav relative to the Galactic frame and produces a diurnal modulation of the line-of-sight- integrated signal. (b) cQED detector comprising a transmon qubit dispersively coupled to a high-Q niobium cavity initialized in a four-component cat state |ψ0⟩. A GDPB mode propagating along ˆk forms an angle Ψ with the cavity axis. (c) Cavity overlap CP(Ψ) for longitudinal (L, blue) and transverse (T, purple) polarizations. The longitudinal and transverse responses are largest at Ψ = 0 and Ψ = π/2, respectively.

FIG. 2. Detector calibration: measured positive-event fraction nmeas versus injected photon number ninj = |β|2 for the six cat-state sizes. Solid curves are the linear fits nmeas = ηα|α|2ninj + δα used to determine the eﬀiciency and false-positive probability.

FIG. 3. Bootstrap distribution of nmeas for a representative search configuration (|α|2 = 1, τ = 4.2 ms). The blue his- togram represents 1000 bootstrap resamples; the red curve is a Gaussian fit (µ ≃0.0148, σ ≃1.3 × 10−3). The Shapiro– Wilk normality test yields p ≃0.09, indicating no statistically significant deviation from a normal distribution at 95% con- fidence.
